edition.alertText: Oil flows top pre-war levels at 24M b/d (Kpler) but VLCC rates hit $1.4M/day; tanker struck off Oman; US orders embassy staff out of Saudi Arabia; Iran vows not a gram of uranium leaves

situation: The Strait of Hormuz crisis entered day 236 with oil flows paradoxically surging above pre-war levels even as Iran intensified attacks and diplomatic channels frayed. Kpler data for the week ending October 18 showed total Middle East oil flows averaging 24.5 million barrels per day — exceeding the 23.3 million bpd pre-war baseline — as Saudi and Emirati pipeline bypasses now handle roughly 40% of non-Iranian crude (up from 17% pre-war). However, Strait of Hormuz transits remain severely depressed: Kpler tracked only about 20 ships completing transit over the past ten days, versus over 100 per day pre-war, while CENTCOM claimed 400 merchant ships passed in the preceding week. UKMTO recorded 135 total incidents since the war began, with 114 confirmed vessel damage reports and 76 people killed or injured. On October 21, a tanker was struck by a projectile 11 nautical miles off Bukha, Oman, causing an engine room fire — all crew were safe. A second tanker was hit off Iraq's Al Faw the previous day. Iran has shifted tactics to infrared-guided missiles targeting engine rooms, with at least 5 engine-room hits in the first two weeks of October alone.

Oil markets climbed on Thursday as Brent crude pushed to $110.29 per barrel (up 1.35%) while WTI rose to $98.32 (up 1.20%), driven by Middle East supply fears, record freight rates, and US inventory draws. VLCC tanker rates have hit a record $1.4 million per day for Gulf-to-East Asia routes (Bloomberg), roughly 47 times the January level of $30,000 per day, with one supertanker reportedly chartered for $82 million on a US Gulf Coast-to-Japan voyage — up 50% from three weeks earlier. Freight now adds approximately $33-41 per barrel to delivered crude cost, representing over 27% of the delivered price versus 3% pre-war. Gold traded near $4,112 per ounce amid safe-haven demand, while Newcastle coal held at $150.55 per tonne as Asian buyers continued substituting away from disrupted Qatar LNG. US diesel prices remain above $6 per gallon, and the US SPR stands at 283 million barrels — its lowest since 1982.

Diplomatic channels remained active but deadlocked as regional tensions widened. Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei declared 'not a single gram of enriched uranium will be removed from Iran,' while Pakistan's army chief Munir continued fifth-round mediation in Tehran — though parliament speaker Ghalibaf told him Iran had 'nothing new' to tell Washington. The US State Department ordered non-essential embassy staff and families to leave Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Jordan, and Bahrain, citing possible renewed hostilities. A Houthi attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed one and injured eight, while drone debris from a Shaybah oilfield interception killed two. The Pentagon is reportedly deploying the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier group to the region, and Trump is weighing post-midterm strike options including Pickaxe Mountain — Iran's underground centrifuge site. Iran's IRGC threatened to cut seven undersea fiber-optic cables running through the Strait of Hormuz. On the supply chain front, Mosaic announced it will idle its South Fort Meade phosphate plant in Florida for over six months starting December 8, citing sulfur shortages above $1,000 per tonne driven by Hormuz disruptions.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 45% from pre-war. Sulfur prices above $1,000/tonne — record highs. Mosaic idling South Fort Meade phosphate plant (Florida) for 6+ months from Dec 8 due to sulfur shortage. US Gulf DAP above $800/st FOB NOLA. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war.

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Urea exports down 83%, ammonia down 75% vs pre-war (ITC data). Bangladesh fertilizer stocks below safe levels — only 2 of 5 urea plants operating. FAO Food Price Index hit 136 in September (highest since Nov 2022). S&P Global warns Hormuz energy shocks + El Niño = global food crisis. CIPS warns double-digit food price rises by Christmas 2026.

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: Qatar LNG exports down 95% from pre-war (ITC). QatarEnergy extended force majeure into November. Asia's JKM gas benchmark 51% above pre-closure levels. Global coal demand forecast to rise 1.2% to record 8.94B tonnes (IEA). Newcastle coal at $150/t as Asian buyers switch from LNG.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint.
